questions.question: A PM offers two explanations for the activation decline: "the new signup flow added friction" and "the AI suggestion prompt confuses people on the empty document." What is wrong with this pair?
options: Both share the assumption that the cause is inside the first session, so they are one explanation in two forms
Neither names a specific user segment
Two explanations are not enough; a decline of this size needs at least four
They are stated as opinions rather than as measured facts
questions.explanation: Competing explanations must disagree about something that matters. Both of these locate the cause inside the first session, so no evidence can separate them from a cause outside it. The tempting distractor is B: missing segmentation is a real weakness, but adding a segment to both explanations still leaves them sharing the same buried assumption.

questions.question: Which of these is a mechanism rather than a relabelled symptom?
options: Performance degrades once a workspace reaches significant scale
Large-workspace users are having a worse experience than small-workspace users
Response times are unacceptable for our highest-value accounts
Workspaces above roughly 500 documents re-check permissions for every document on search, and search runs on page load
questions.explanation: D names actors, a step order, and a trigger, so it predicts things you could check without shipping. A is the tempting distractor because it sounds technical, but "degrades at scale" only restates that the symptom appears in large workspaces. No observation could rule it out.

questions.question: You believe large-workspace slowness comes from permission re-checks during search. What makes this belief testable before any code is written?
options: Estimating how many engineering days the fix would take
A side prediction it makes about something you have not looked at yet — for example, that slow sessions should cluster on search-heavy usage rather than on document opens
Confirming that the 34% rise is statistically significant
Getting the engineering lead to agree the theory is consistent with the codebase
questions.explanation: A mechanism earns its place by predicting something beyond the symptom it was invented to explain. B names an observation that could come back the wrong way. D is the tempting distractor: expert agreement raises plausibility, and plausibility is exactly what makes a wrong mechanism hard to displace.

questions.question: No support ticket has ever mentioned speed, but monitoring shows a 34% P95 rise for large workspaces. How should this absence be treated?
options: As proof that the monitoring signal is a measurement artifact and no user is affected
As irrelevant, since behavioural data always outranks self-reported complaints
As evidence that has to be assigned to a mechanism — it damages some explanations and supports others, and you must say which
As a reason to survey large-workspace users before doing any other analysis
questions.explanation: Silence discriminates. It counts against any mechanism in which users notice and suffer, and it is consistent with one in which the rise sits in rare or background requests. A is the tempting distractor: it takes a single consistent explanation and treats it as the only one, which is the same shortcut that produces wrong tickets.

questions.question: A cheap, reversible change would help under every mechanism your team has written down. What does the model say to do?
options: Hold the change until the mechanism is established, because acting without a mechanism is what this lesson warns against
Ship it and observe, because distinguishing mechanisms buys nothing when the action does not change
Ship it and record it as confirmation of the most likely mechanism if the metric improves
Split the change into variants, one per mechanism, and run them against each other
questions.explanation: This is the boundary of the model. Diagnosis is worth its cost only when different mechanisms would lead to different actions. A is the tempting distractor because it applies the rule correctly in the wrong situation, turning rigour into procedure. C also fails: a change that helps under every mechanism confirms none of them.
